help.body:
**Continuous work lets Aeon pick up ready work by itself.** Normally a loop starts when you start it. With this switched on, a scheduler looks at the repositories you enrolled, finds work that is ready (queue and roadmap items) and starts a loop for it — without anyone asking at that moment.

### How it decides
Every few seconds the scheduler runs a *tick*. For each enrolled repository it checks, in order: is the master on and not paused, is the repository enabled, does its template load, is the time inside its window, is the repository already busy, is there budget left, is there ready work. The first check that fails is the **reason** shown next to the repository. The **Next tick** tab runs that same check without starting anything.

### What you control
- **Master switch** — off until you turn it on. Turning it on confirms with exactly what you are granting.
- **Pause** — stops picking new work; loops already running keep running. **Stop everything** pauses and also stops the running loops.
- **Repositories** — only enrolled, enabled repositories are touched. Each has a blueprint (the loop to run), a minimum priority and a time window.
- **Slots** — a cap on how many loops run at once.

### Safe by construction
Loops started this way run **unattended**: an action that would need a person''s approval is denied on the spot, so they cannot open or merge a pull request on their own. When a loop is blocked and needs you, it shows up under **Needs you**.

Every act on this page is audited to the person who did it.
